example_pt: Onde fica o hotel? O hotel fica na praia.
example_en: Where is the hotel (located)? The hotel is on the beach. (a fixed place)

example_pt: Eu fico no hotel. Fico feliz.
example_en: I’m staying at the hotel. I become / end up happy.

example_pt: Onde está a mala? Ela está no hotel.
example_en: Where is the suitcase? She is at the hotel (right now).
I’m well (right now).

example_pt: Ela é brasileira. Você é americano?
example_en: She is Brazilian. Are you American? (identity)
It’s three o’clock. (time uses ser)
She is in Brazil (right now, not “she is Brazilian”).
I’m well (a state right now).
What is this (here, by me)?
What is that (by you)? — and, casually, this/that in general.
What is that over there (away from both of us)?
Who is it? (a person)
What is that? (a thing)

example_pt: Sou de Nova York. De onde você é?
example_en: I’m from New York. Where are you from?

example_pt: Estou em Nova York. Estou no hotel.
example_en: I’m in New York. I’m at the hotel.

example_pt: É um bom hotel. Boa tarde!
example_en: It’s a good hotel. Good afternoon! (adjective; agrees)
I’m well. Everything all right? (adverb; does not agree)
Good afternoon! It’s late. (afternoon, or the word “late”)
Good evening / good night. (once it’s dark, or as a goodbye at night)
Are you American? (everyday “you”)
Are you American? (formal, respectful “you”)
